definition: Harsh or irritating in manner; also physically rough.
sentence: The abrasive waiter didn't merely say the soup was unavailable; he implied my ancestors were foolish for wanting soup in the first place.

definition: To reduce the force, effect, or intensity of something.
sentence: I tried to attenuate the bagpipe noise by closing the window, hiding under a blanket, and briefly considering relocation to Antarctica.

definition: Grief or mourning after the death of someone close.
sentence: During his bereavement, Uncle Fred wore black, spoke softly, and somehow inherited seventeen extremely loud parrots.

definition: Something very helpful or beneficial.
sentence: The invention of stretchy pants was a boon to everyone who had ever said, 'Yes, I would like dessert.'

definition: To limit, restrict, or define the boundaries of something.
sentence: Mom circumscribed my 'small birthday party' to twelve guests after I attempted to invite the entire marching band.

definition: Corresponding appropriately in size, degree, or proportion.
sentence: My allowance was not commensurate with the heroic suffering involved in unloading a dishwasher containing three whole forks.

definition: A large destructive fire; figuratively, a major violent conflict.
sentence: One forgotten pizza in the oven produced a conflagration impressive enough that the smoke detector seemed personally offended.

definition: Easy to see or notice; attracting attention.
sentence: Wearing a sequined tuxedo to the dentist made Kevin conspicuous, especially when the disco ball hat began spinning.

definition: To interpret something in a particular way.
sentence: Please do not construe my screaming and sprinting from the room as criticism of your pet tarantula.

definition: To violate or conflict with a law, rule, or principle.
sentence: Bringing a live goat into chemistry class contravened at least four school rules and one deeply reasonable fire code.

definition: The act of throwing someone or something out of a window.
sentence: The defenestration of the printer occurred shortly after it announced, for the ninth time, that there was a 'paper jam' despite containing no paper.

definition: To establish or mark the limits of something.
sentence: Dad used orange cones to delimit the part of the driveway where my brother was absolutely forbidden to practice flaming-javelin juggling.

definition: To mark or establish a boundary or distinction.
sentence: A line of rubber ducks demarcated my sister's half of the bedroom after diplomatic negotiations collapsed.

definition: Emotionally uninvolved or objective; also physically separate.
sentence: The referee remained detached while two parents argued passionately over whether a six-year-old had committed 'an outrageous injustice against soccer.'

definition: Intended to teach, sometimes in an overly preachy way.
sentence: Grandpa's didactic story about fiscal responsibility began with a nickel in 1957 and somehow lasted until lunch.

definition: Fundamentally different or distinct in kind.
sentence: The talent show featured disparate acts: opera, chainsaw sculpture, and a boy who claimed he could communicate telepathically with hamsters.

definition: To cause or give rise to something.
sentence: The principal's announcement of a surprise six-hour assembly engendered a level of despair usually reserved for shipwrecks.

definition: To establish so firmly that change becomes difficult.
sentence: Grandma's habit of hiding cash in cereal boxes became so entrenched that breakfast required a financial audit.

definition: Exacting means demanding great care or effort; to exact means to demand or obtain something, often forcefully.
sentence: The exacting piano teacher demanded perfect scales, then exacted payment in the form of cash and one suspiciously large lemon tart.

definition: Joking about something serious, often inappropriately.
sentence: When the canoe sprang a leak, Marcus facetiously asked whether anyone had brought a submarine.

definition: Very attentive to detail and cleanliness; hard to please.
sentence: The fastidious cat refused to sit on the couch until I removed one crumb, two hairs, and what he considered an unacceptable decorative pillow.

definition: Unable to both be true or happen at the same time.
sentence: My goals of 'eat the entire cake' and 'save the entire cake for tomorrow' were, tragically, mutually exclusive.

definition: The lowest or worst point.
sentence: My culinary career reached its nadir when the smoke alarm applauded my grilled cheese before I did.

definition: Spread throughout something; widespread.
sentence: The smell of burnt popcorn was so pervasive that even the goldfish looked annoyed.

definition: To suggest or assume something as a basis for reasoning.
sentence: I postulate that the missing cookies were eaten by Dad, based on the crumbs in his beard and his refusal to testify.

definition: To meet requirements; or to limit or modify a statement.
sentence: I qualified for the pie-eating contest, though I should qualify that statement by admitting there were only two contestants and the other was a toddler.

definition: Most noticeable, important, or relevant.
sentence: The salient feature of Trevor's presentation was not the chart; it was the raccoon quietly eating his laser pointer.

definition: To officially permit or approve; paradoxically, also to impose a penalty for wrongdoing.
sentence: The league sanctioned the mascot race but threatened sanctions after the eagle mascot tackled the hot dog at midfield.

definition: False, fake, or not based on valid reasoning.
sentence: His spurious claim that homework causes baldness collapsed when the teacher asked why he still had so much hair.

definition: Understood or implied without being directly stated.
sentence: There was a tacit agreement not to mention Dad's karaoke performance, especially while the neighbors were still filing complaints.

definition: Clear and leaving no doubt.
sentence: Mom's unequivocal answer to 'Can I keep this raccoon?' was 'No,' followed by several additional noes for emphasis.

definition: To become less intense or widespread.
sentence: The applause finally abated when everyone realized the 'famous actor' was just Uncle Steve in sunglasses.

definition: A departure from what is normal or expected.
sentence: My brother cleaning his room voluntarily was such an aberration that we checked him for fever.

definition: To shorten a text without losing its main meaning.
sentence: I abridged my twelve-page apology to 'Sorry about the llama,' which everyone agreed captured the essentials.

definition: Difficult to understand; obscure.
sentence: The professor's abstruse explanation of quantum mechanics left me understanding only that particles are apparently very indecisive.

definition: Agreement or harmony; also to grant or give.
sentence: The siblings reached an accord: Mia got the top bunk, and Leo was accorded the sacred right to control the night-light.

definition: To accept something reluctantly but without protest.
sentence: After forty-seven minutes of begging, Dad acquiesced and allowed the inflatable dinosaur to sit at the dinner table.

definition: To declare someone not guilty of a crime or accusation.
sentence: The jury acquitted the dog of stealing the steak after compelling evidence showed the cat wearing barbecue sauce.

definition: Bitter anger or hostility.
sentence: The family Monopoly game ended in acrimony after Grandma built hotels, bankrupted everyone, and demanded respect for her 'business instincts.'

definition: To cause a machine or process to operate; to put into action.
sentence: Pressing the red button actuated the robot, which immediately stole my sandwich and declared itself management.

definition: Old, well-known sayings expressing general truths.
sentence: Grandpa communicated almost entirely in adages, including several he clearly invented while losing at checkers.

definition: To make something poorer or impure by adding an inferior substance.
sentence: My cousin adulterated the chili with chocolate syrup and then had the nerve to call himself an innovator.

definition: The arrival or beginning of an important event, person, or thing.
sentence: With the advent of group chats, teenagers gained the ability to misunderstand one another at unprecedented speed.

definition: Artificial, pretentious, or deliberately adopted rather than natural.
sentence: His affected British accent vanished the instant he stubbed his toe and shouted in pure New Jersey.

definition: A total formed by combining separate things; also to combine them.
sentence: In the aggregate, the twins owned 143 stuffed animals, nine of which had somehow been elected to public office.

definition: Alter means to change; an altar is a raised or sacred table used in worship or ceremony.
sentence: The tailor altered my suit; thankfully, he did not place it on an altar and begin chanting over the sleeves.

definition: Able to walk; relating to walking or outpatient care.
sentence: The doctor declared Grandpa ambulatory moments before Grandpa sprinted down the hallway chasing the pudding cart.

definition: Willing to agree or cooperate; responsive to influence.
sentence: The principal was amenable to our proposal until he reached the sentence involving a cafeteria zip line.

definition: Friendly relations or peaceful harmony.
sentence: Years of sibling warfare ended in amity when both children discovered a common enemy: the new babysitter's vegetable casserole.

definition: Without a clear shape, structure, or organization.
sentence: The 'sculpture' was an amorphous blob of clay that I confidently titled 'Tax Season.'

definition: Agreement or approval, especially after consideration.
sentence: Dad gave his assent to the sleepover after making us sign a treaty banning indoor hockey.

definition: To make something larger or greater by adding to it.
sentence: I augmented my résumé by adding 'advanced dragon negotiation,' which may have been a strategic mistake.

definition: Suggesting that future success is likely; favorable.
sentence: The wedding had an auspicious start when the ring was found, the cake remained upright, and no peacocks escaped.

definition: New, experimental, and unconventional, especially in art.
sentence: The chef called his ketchup-on-ice-cream creation avant-garde; the children called it a cry for help.

definition: So ordinary or overused that it is boring.
sentence: His speech was so banal that even the motivational poster seemed to roll its eyes.

definition: To trouble, harass, or surround with difficulties.
sentence: The beleaguered substitute teacher faced thirty students, a broken projector, and a hamster with suspicious leadership skills.

definition: Using grand, inflated language with little substance.
sentence: The mayor's bombastic speech described the new parking meter as 'a monumental triumph of human civilization.'

definition: A person who performs tasks clumsily or incompetently.
sentence: The bungler hired to fix the sink somehow disabled the doorbell and improved the toaster.

definition: Able to float; cheerful and optimistic.
sentence: Despite falling into the pool fully dressed, Clara remained buoyant both physically and emotionally.

definition: To support, strengthen, or reinforce.
sentence: Dad buttressed his argument that we needed a puppy with charts, expert testimony, and a PowerPoint titled 'Operation Fluffy.'

definition: Changing suddenly and unpredictably.
sentence: The capricious toddler loved bananas on Monday, despised them Tuesday, and by Wednesday demanded they be addressed as 'Your Majesty.'

definition: To criticize or punish severely.
sentence: The coach castigated us for arriving late as though we'd delayed the moon landing rather than seventh-grade soccer practice.

definition: Longer and less direct than necessary.
sentence: Dad took a circuitous route to avoid traffic and somehow drove us through three states and a llama festival.

definition: Careful consideration of risks before acting.
sentence: With admirable circumspection, Maya asked whether launching a potato cannon indoors might have consequences.

definition: Aware or conscious of something.
sentence: I was cognizant of the 'Do Not Feed the Bears' sign, but the bear appeared extremely cognizant of my sandwich.

definition: Able to catch fire and burn easily.
sentence: The science teacher calmly moved the combustible materials away from Ethan, who had already asked whether eyebrows grow back.

definition: Spacious and comfortable.
sentence: The hamster's new cage was so commodious that it had a breakfast nook and better closet space than my apartment.

definition: To calm hostility and restore goodwill.
sentence: I tried to conciliate the furious twins by offering each an identical cookie and appointing the dog as neutral mediator.

definition: Agreement or harmony between people or groups.
sentence: Peace and concord returned to the car once everyone agreed that Dad's playlist was a human-rights violation.

definition: To argue or assert; also to compete or struggle.
sentence: My brother contended that he deserved the last brownie because he had 'suffered greatly,' meaning he had waited almost six minutes.

definition: To confirm or support a statement with additional evidence.
sentence: Three witnesses corroborated my story that the dog opened the refrigerator, though all three witnesses were also dogs.

definition: Shaped into alternating ridges and grooves.
sentence: The corrugated cardboard box looked ordinary until Grandma announced it was my cousin's new 'budget sports car.'

definition: To lower the quality, value, dignity, or character of something.
sentence: The museum director said putting googly eyes on the marble bust would debase the collection; I maintain it improved morale.

definition: To publicly condemn or criticize.
sentence: The neighborhood association decried leaf blowers with the passion usually reserved for invading armies.

definition: Respectful submission to another person's judgment or authority.
sentence: Out of deference to Grandma, everyone pretended her brick-like fruitcake was 'delightfully substantial.'

definition: To clearly mark a boundary or distinction.
sentence: Yellow tape demarcated the kitchen after Dad's attempt at flambé created what the fire department called 'a learning opportunity.'

definition: Extreme moral corruption or wickedness.
sentence: Stealing one cookie was naughty; stealing the entire tray and blaming the baby was, according to Grandma, depravity.

definition: To express disapproval of; to belittle or play down.
sentence: She deprecated her own artistic talent while standing beside a portrait so good that the dog barked at it.

definition: To treat something sacred or respected with violent disrespect.
sentence: Putting a soda cup on Grandma's antique piano was treated as an act of desecration requiring immediate family court.

definition: To remove moisture from; to dry out thoroughly.
sentence: The forgotten muffin had desiccated into an object suitable for either geology class or self-defense.

definition: Extremely discouraged, sad, or without hope.
sentence: I became despondent when the ice-cream truck drove past me, then circled back only to serve the neighbor's dog.

definition: Lacking a plan, purpose, or steady effort; jumping from one thing to another.
sentence: My desultory cleaning involved folding one sock, reading a comic, watering a spoon, and declaring the room improved.

definition: Precisely fixed, defined, or limited.
sentence: The meeting had a determinate end time because at 6:00 the building was hosting competitive ferret yoga.

definition: A long, bitter, angry speech or piece of writing.
sentence: Dad launched into a twenty-minute diatribe about people who leave one teaspoon of milk in the carton.

definition: Modesty or shyness caused by lack of self-confidence.
sentence: Despite her diffidence, Nora eventually whispered her brilliant answer while the loudest student confidently explained why dolphins are fish.

definition: A difference or inconsistency between things that should agree.
sentence: There was a discrepancy between my brother's claim of eating 'one cookie' and the seventeen wrappers in his pockets.

definition: Moving from topic to topic rather than staying tightly focused.
sentence: Grandpa's discursive toast began with the bride, wandered through lawn care, and ended with a warning about raccoons.

definition: Not influenced by strong emotion; impartial.
sentence: The judge gave a dispassionate ruling on the disputed cupcake while both children sobbed like exiled monarchs.

definition: To send off quickly for a purpose; also to deal with promptly.
sentence: Mom dispatched me to the store for milk, and I dispatched the errand in six minutes until I remembered I had bought orange juice.

definition: A state of having a bad reputation.
sentence: The restaurant fell into disrepute after its slogan changed to 'Probably Soup.'

definition: A lack of harmony or agreement; harsh-sounding musical combinations.
sentence: There was striking dissonance between the choir's angelic melody and the tuba player's decision to perform the theme from Jaws.

definition: To swell or expand because of pressure from inside.
sentence: After Thanksgiving dinner, my stomach seemed to distend until my belt filed a formal complaint.

definition: Extremely harsh or severe.
sentence: The teacher's draconian policy imposed detention for forgetting a pencil and exile for misplacing an eraser.

definition: Deceitful by pretending one thing while doing another.
sentence: The duplicitous cat purred affectionately while slowly pushing my water glass toward the edge of the table.

definition: An official order or proclamation issued by an authority.
sentence: Dad issued an edict banning glitter after discovering it in his shoes, wallet, soup, and apparently bloodstream.

definition: Abnormally thin or weak, especially from lack of food.
sentence: The actor looked emaciated for the role, while his pampered pug looked like it owned several restaurants.

definition: To involve someone deeply in a conflict or difficult situation.
sentence: I became embroiled in the neighborhood feud after innocently asking whose garden gnome was wearing my hat.

definition: Deep hostility or hatred.
sentence: A state of permanent enmity existed between our cat and the vacuum cleaner.

definition: Artificial and inferior; a substitute imitation.
sentence: The motel served ersatz maple syrup so suspicious that even the pancakes seemed embarrassed.

definition: A mild expression used instead of one considered harsh or unpleasant.
sentence: Calling Dad's snoring 'nighttime thunder' was a generous euphemism that fooled absolutely nobody.

definition: Pleasant and smooth-sounding.
sentence: The word 'mellifluous' sounded euphonious until my brother repeated it forty-seven times in the car.

definition: Quickly fading or disappearing.
sentence: My determination to diet was evanescent; it vanished the moment someone opened a box of doughnuts.

definition: To dig up something buried, especially a corpse.
sentence: We exhumed the time capsule and discovered that our 2009 predictions involved flying cars and an alarming amount of Silly Bandz.

definition: Coming from outside rather than being inherent.
sentence: The trophy provided extrinsic motivation; my intrinsic motivation was mainly to beat Trevor, who had been smug since breakfast.

definition: Plowed but left unseeded; inactive or undeveloped for a time.
sentence: My exercise plan lay fallow all winter while my couch enjoyed unprecedented prosperity.

definition: Extreme, unquestioning enthusiasm or zeal.
sentence: His fanaticism about barbecue sauce became apparent when he brought six bottles to a wedding and ranked the hors d'oeuvres by 'sauce compatibility.'

definition: Having an extremely unpleasant smell.
sentence: The fetid gym bag had developed an odor so powerful that TSA asked it for identification.

definition: To restrain or restrict, literally or figuratively.
sentence: School rules fettered my entrepreneurial plan to sell espresso shots during kindergarten recess.

definition: A complete and embarrassing failure.
sentence: The surprise party became a fiasco when we surprised the wrong Mr. Jenkins and he stayed for cake anyway.

definition: A person who passionately stirs up change or conflict.
sentence: The twelve-year-old firebrand demanded longer recess, cheaper cookies, and immediate recognition of the cafeteria workers' accordion band.

definition: Irregular, intermittent, or restless.
sentence: I got fitful sleep because the hotel air conditioner alternated between roaring like a jet and becoming mysteriously silent.

definition: To openly disregard a rule, law, or convention.
sentence: My uncle flouted the 'formal attire' rule by arriving at the wedding in swim fins and a bow tie.

definition: To prevent or delay something by acting in advance.
sentence: I ate a snack to forestall hunger and accidentally forestalled dinner by consuming an entire lasagna.

definition: Bold and irritating nerve; also bitterness.
sentence: He had the gall to borrow my car, return it empty, and complain that I had chosen an inconvenient gas gauge.

definition: To shock or excite someone into taking action.
sentence: The announcement that the pizza shop was closing galvanized the neighborhood into organizing its fastest protest in recorded history.

definition: Clever deceit or sly cunning.
sentence: With remarkable guile, the toddler distracted us by pointing at the ceiling while stealing three cupcakes.

definition: Overused and unoriginal.
sentence: The movie's hackneyed ending featured a slow clap, a sunset, and someone saying, 'Maybe the real treasure was friendship.'

definition: A person who challenges cherished beliefs or traditions.
sentence: The family iconoclast suggested replacing Thanksgiving turkey with tacos and was nearly written out of the will.

definition: Having little or no money.
sentence: After buying concert tickets, I was so impecunious that I compared prices on individual grains of rice.

definition: To drive or urge someone to act.
sentence: The smell of fresh cinnamon rolls impelled me toward the kitchen with the speed of a highly motivated gazelle.

definition: Arrogantly commanding and expecting obedience.
sentence: My cat gave an imperious meow that clearly meant, 'Open the tuna now, peasant.'

definition: Unable to be affected, penetrated, or harmed.
sentence: Grandpa was impervious to embarrassment and wore his 'World's Hottest Grandpa' shirt to the parent-teacher conference.

definition: Acting suddenly without enough thought.
sentence: In an impetuous moment, Leo bought a unicycle online despite having neither balance nor any known reason to own one.

definition: A force or reason that makes something happen faster.
sentence: The discovery of a mouse provided tremendous impetus for cleaning the kitchen.

definition: Clear, sharp, and intelligently analytical.
sentence: Her incisive question—'Why is there a goat in the conference room?'—cut directly to the central problem.

definition: Impossible or very difficult to correct or reform.
sentence: My incorrigible uncle still hides plastic spiders in the sugar bowl despite twenty years of family sanctions.

definition: Impossible to remove, erase, or forget.
sentence: The purple dye left an indelible mark on the carpet and an even more indelible mark on Dad's emotional life.

definition: Extremely annoying or hellish; relating to hell.
sentence: That infernal smoke detector chirped every forty seconds until I began negotiating with it personally.

definition: Impossible or very difficult to understand.
sentence: The cat's expression was inscrutable as he stared at the wall for eleven minutes and then attacked a sock.

definition: Lacking flavor, vigor, or interest.
sentence: The soup was so insipid that the salt shaker requested permission to intervene.

definition: Unable to pay debts owed.
sentence: After opening a lemonade stand with marble counters and valet parking, the eight-year-old entrepreneur was insolvent by noon.

definition: To cause or provoke an event or action, often trouble.
sentence: My cousin instigated the food fight by launching one pea and whispering, 'History will remember us.'

definition: Narrow-minded or isolated from outside ideas or influences.
sentence: The club became so insular that members regarded people from the next hallway as mysterious foreigners.

definition: To bury a dead body.
sentence: We interred the deceased goldfish with full honors, a tiny shoebox, and a eulogy that lasted longer than its life.

definition: To overwhelm with a flood or huge amount of something.
sentence: After posting a puppy photo, I was inundated with messages from relatives who had ignored me for months.

definition: Abusive or insulting language.
sentence: The coach unleashed a torrent of invective at the broken vending machine, which remained emotionally unaffected.

definition: Easily angered or bad-tempered.
sentence: Our irascible neighbor once yelled at a cloud for 'looking suspicious.'

definition: To throw away or discard something, especially to lighten a load.
sentence: To make room in the car, Dad jettisoned three beach chairs, a broken umbrella, and somehow my left shoe.

definition: Fond of joking; humorous and playful.
sentence: The jocular dentist called the drill 'Mr. Buzzy,' which did not improve Mr. Buzzy's reputation.

definition: Weak, unconvincing, or unsatisfactory; traditionally also unable to walk normally.
sentence: 'My hamster ate my homework' was a lame excuse, especially because I do not own a hamster.

definition: The unlawful taking of someone else's personal property.
sentence: The toddler's cookie larceny was captured on camera, along with his attempt to hide the evidence in his socks.

definition: Rich, abundant, and growing thickly.
sentence: After one humid week, the garden became so luxuriant that we lost a lawn chair and possibly an uncle.

definition: Clumsy, awkward, or tactless.
sentence: His maladroit attempt at romance involved stepping on her foot, spilling soup, and complimenting her 'surprisingly normal elbows.'

definition: Changing mood or behavior quickly and unpredictably.
sentence: The mercurial chef praised my omelet, insulted the pan, hugged a carrot, and resigned before breakfast ended.

definition: To trap or become stuck in a difficult situation; also swampy ground.
sentence: Our committee became mired in a forty-minute debate over whether the meeting snacks counted as 'strategic resources.'

definition: A person who dislikes or distrusts humankind.
sentence: The neighborhood misanthrope installed a welcome mat reading, 'You Have Made a Mistake.'

definition: To calm someone's anger or anxiety.
sentence: I tried to mollify Dad after denting the car by pointing out that the dent was remarkably symmetrical.

definition: A newly invented word or expression.
sentence: My sister's neologism 'snackcident' describes accidentally eating an entire family-size bag of chips.
synonyms: coinage; new word; newly coined term

definition: To make something unclear or harder to understand.
sentence: The politician obfuscated his answer so thoroughly that by the end we were discussing turnips and no one remembered the question.

definition: Noticeably intrusive or difficult to ignore.
sentence: The waiter was unobtrusive; the mariachi band following him to every table was decidedly obtrusive.

definition: Great wealth, luxury, or abundance.
sentence: The hamster cage's opulence included velvet bedding, a chandelier, and a tiny portrait of the hamster itself.

definition: Apparently or supposedly, though perhaps not actually.
sentence: We went to the mall ostensibly to buy socks, but somehow returned with a kayak.

definition: Designed to impress by showing off wealth, knowledge, or importance.
sentence: His ostentatious pencil case was gold-plated, monogrammed, and opened with its own theme music.

definition: A surface layer or appearance that develops with age or use.
sentence: The antique desk had a lovely patina; my desk had a similar effect created mostly by spilled coffee.

definition: A strong or habitual liking for something.
sentence: Grandma has a penchant for dramatic hats, particularly ones capable of blocking satellite signals.

definition: Continuing or recurring for a very long time; year after year.
sentence: Our team is perennially optimistic in September and perennially discussing 'next season' by October.

definition: Done with minimal effort, interest, or care.
sentence: He gave the dishes a perfunctory rinse that somehow left the spaghetti exactly where it had started.

definition: Extreme unwillingness to spend money or use resources.
sentence: Grandpa's parsimony reached new heights when he cut a paper towel into eight 'perfectly adequate' napkins.

definition: Having keen judgment and insight.
sentence: The perspicacious toddler immediately realized that adults saying 'maybe later' meant 'absolutely never.'

definition: Childishly sulky or bad-tempered.
sentence: The petulant CEO crossed his arms and refused to continue the meeting because someone took his favorite swivel chair.

definition: Devout religious reverence; also dutiful respect.
sentence: Grandma's piety was unquestioned, though even she briefly lost composure when the choir director started beatboxing.

definition: To make someone less angry or hostile.
sentence: We placated the furious toddler with crackers, a sticker, and temporary control of the family government.

definition: Sounding sad, mournful, or wistful.
sentence: The dog's plaintive whine suggested he had not eaten in years, despite the kibble visibly stuck to his nose.

definition: A large or abundant supply.
sentence: The buffet offered a plenitude of desserts, and I approached it with the solemn focus of an Olympic athlete.

definition: To indicate that something, usually significant or unpleasant, is likely to happen.
sentence: The sudden silence from the children's room portended either sleep or an insurance claim.

definition: To prevent something from happening or make it impossible.
sentence: My complete lack of rhythm did not preclude me from dancing; it merely precluded everyone else from enjoying it.

definition: Preventing something from happening or making it impossible.
sentence: The broken elevator was precluding Grandma's dramatic entrance, so she used the stairs and arrived even more dramatically.

definition: Showing unusually advanced ability at a young age.
sentence: The precocious five-year-old corrected my grammar, explained compound interest, and then demanded dinosaur-shaped pasta.

definition: A preference or special liking for something.
sentence: My uncle's predilection for Hawaiian shirts makes every family photo look like a tropical emergency.

definition: Superior to or more important than all others.
sentence: Professor Whiskers was the preeminent expert on cardboard boxes, mostly because he was a cat and had conducted years of fieldwork.

definition: Having knowledge or foresight about what will happen.
sentence: Mom looked prescient when she packed extra towels, snacks, batteries, and apparently everything needed for a minor apocalypse.

definition: Wastefully extravagant with money or resources.
sentence: My prodigal cousin spent his entire allowance on a fog machine for his bedroom and then asked to borrow bus fare.

definition: Remarkably great in size, amount, or degree.
sentence: The toddler produced a prodigious quantity of spaghetti from places no spaghetti should have been.

definition: A person or business that supplies or sells something.
sentence: The corner shop is a purveyor of fine chocolates, mediocre umbrellas, and inexplicably aggressive greeting cards.

definition: Feelings of doubt, uneasiness, or moral concern about something.
sentence: I had qualms about eating the mystery casserole after the chef whispered, 'Don't ask what the crunchy part is.'

definition: A difficult situation requiring a choice between options.
sentence: I faced a quandary: admit I broke the vase or let everyone continue blaming the extremely innocent-looking dog.

definition: Deep, lasting bitterness or resentment.
sentence: Years of rancor divided the two neighbors over a dispute that began with one borrowed wheelbarrow in 1998.

definition: A long, slender, sharply pointed sword; figuratively, something sharply witty.
sentence: Her rapier wit ended the argument with one sentence and left three uncles quietly reconsidering their lives.

definition: To completely destroy a building or structure.
sentence: The developers razed the old shed, disappointing the raccoon family that had recently renovated the attic.

definition: To publicly withdraw a statement or belief.
sentence: I recanted my claim that assembling the bookshelf would be 'easy' approximately three screws and one existential crisis later.

definition: To remedy or correct a wrong; also compensation for a wrong.
sentence: The hotel offered free breakfast to redress the injustice of assigning us a room directly beside the accordion convention.

definition: Deserving strong condemnation; morally very wrong.
sentence: Stealing Grandma's pie was reprehensible; returning the empty dish and asking for whipped cream was somehow worse.

definition: A temporary delay or escape from punishment or difficulty.
sentence: The canceled math test gave us a reprieve, though the teacher ominously called it 'merely a postponement of destiny.'

definition: To criticize or correct someone for wrongdoing.
sentence: Mom reproved the dog for stealing dinner, while the dog stared solemnly at the cat as if preparing an appeal.

definition: To reject, deny, or refuse to accept something.
sentence: After tasting the neon-green casserole, even its creator repudiated it and ordered pizza.

definition: Excessively sweet, either in taste or sentiment.
sentence: The movie's saccharine ending featured puppies, rainbows, a group hug, and a spontaneous choir singing about friendship.

definition: To fully satisfy a desire or appetite.
sentence: I attempted to sate my hunger with one cookie and conducted additional research using eleven more.

definition: Very careful to do things correctly and ethically.
sentence: The scrupulous cashier returned the extra penny, documented the incident, and probably notified the Treasury.

definition: Showing sharp practical judgment.
sentence: The shrewd eight-year-old sold lemonade beside the marathon finish line and accepted cash, cards, and 'desperate promises.'

definition: Having many smooth curves or bends.
sentence: The sinuous garden path wound so dramatically that reaching the mailbox felt like crossing the Andes.

definition: Done carelessly and too quickly.
sentence: His slapdash repair involved duct tape, chewing gum, and the phrase 'Nobody touch the ceiling fan.'

definition: Serious, formal, and dignified.
sentence: With solemn faces, the children buried the broken remote control and observed seven seconds of silence.

definition: Very simple, austere, and lacking comfort or luxury.
sentence: The hotel room was spartan: one bed, one chair, and a decorative painting that appeared to apologize.

definition: To reject someone or something with contempt.
sentence: The cat spurned the expensive salmon and ate a dust bunny from beneath the refrigerator.

definition: Loyal, dependable, and strong; a devoted supporter.
sentence: Our stalwart babysitter remained calm through a power outage, a plumbing leak, and the toddler declaring himself emperor.

definition: A grouped set of lines in a poem.
sentence: My poem's final stanza rhymed 'orange' with 'door hinge,' causing the English teacher to age visibly.

definition: A state in which there is little or no change or movement.
sentence: Negotiations reached stasis when both siblings refused to surrender the blue cup, despite six identical cups nearby.

definition: Free from living microorganisms; also lacking creativity or vitality.
sentence: The laboratory was sterile; my brother's bedroom appeared to be conducting the opposite experiment.

definition: Loud, harsh, and forceful.
sentence: A strident voice from the back seat demanded to know whether we were there yet, fourteen seconds after departure.

definition: To block, hinder, or prevent progress.
sentence: My plan to become a world-famous chef was stymied by the discovery that boiling water requires attention.

definition: Flexible and able to bend easily; adaptable.
sentence: The yoga instructor was supple enough to fold herself like a paper clip; I was supple enough to reach one sock.

definition: Bad-tempered and unfriendly.
sentence: The surly barista wrote 'Probably Brian' on my cup and sighed as though coffee itself had betrayed him.

definition: Secretive, especially because discovery would cause trouble.
sentence: My surreptitious midnight trip to the refrigerator failed when the cheese drawer squeaked like a haunted violin.

definition: Equivalent in effect or seriousness.
sentence: For my grandmother, declining a second helping was tantamount to declaring war on the family.

definition: Excessive boldness or nerve.
sentence: He had the temerity to correct Grandma's lasagna recipe while actively eating his third serving.

definition: Very weak, slight, or uncertain.
sentence: My tenuous excuse for being late involved a squirrel, a drawbridge, and several events that do not occur in our state.

definition: A state of physical or mental inactivity or sluggishness.
sentence: After Thanksgiving dinner, the entire family entered a state of torpor broken only by the distant sound of pie being served.

definition: Awkward, clumsy, or difficult to handle.
sentence: The ungainly inflatable flamingo required four adults, two ropes, and an apology to the neighbor's hedge.

definition: Not aware of what one is doing or of the full facts.
sentence: I became the unwitting accomplice in my niece's cookie theft when she hid the evidence in my coat pocket.

definition: To regard with very great respect or reverence.
sentence: My family venerates Grandma's secret cookie recipe, though Grandma insists the secret is 'following the directions on the bag.'

definition: The appearance of being true or real.
sentence: The cardboard spaceship had surprising verisimilitude until the captain's mother called him inside for dinner.

definition: Watchful and alert for danger or problems.
sentence: The vigilant lifeguard noticed every unsafe swimmer except the duck repeatedly stealing French fries.

definition: A person with exceptional skill, especially in music or art.
sentence: The piano virtuoso played Chopin flawlessly while I contributed by turning pages at several completely wrong moments.

definition: Extremely harmful, hostile, or poisonous; especially severe of a disease or criticism.
sentence: The review was so virulent that the restaurant's bread basket may have needed therapy.

definition: Full of harsh, abusive criticism.
sentence: The losing candidate's vituperous speech accused the bake-sale judges of corruption, incompetence, and suspicious loyalty to brownies.

definition: Deliberate and intentional, especially stubbornly disobedient.
sentence: The dog's destruction of the couch looked willful; he paused halfway through to make eye contact.

definition: Showing intense enthusiasm or devotion.
sentence: The zealous crossing guard treated our quiet cul-de-sac like the final checkpoint in an international security operation.
